mike_r: Quick heads-up — ran an attention-kernel sweep across H100 / A100 / L40S. Seq sweep 128..8192, batch sizes 1/4/8. Observed a regression on H100 starting at seq >= 4096 when KV cache is enabled. Artifacts: s3://rwd-infer-perf/1798129999/

sara: can you paste the numbers? :eyes:

mike_r: pasted the condensed table below (TL;DR: big spike on H100 at 4k+ with KV active)

```
HW   SEQ   BATCH   kernel    latency(ms)/step
H100  512     1    fused2     0.45
H100  512     8    fused2     0.52
H100 2048     1    flashv2    1.8
H100 2048     8    flashv2    2.1
H100 4096     4    paged     12.4   <-- spike when KV enabled (host memcpy observed)
H100 8192     8    paged     34.2   (KV spill to host)
A100 4096     4    paged      9.1
L40S 4096     4    paged     10.3
```

mike_r: nvprof/profiler indicates a surge of cudaMemcpyAsync host <-> device and long kernel queue stalls on H100 at 4k+. KV cache footprint crosses ~1.2GB and triggers host-side spill.

jin: is this regression new vs last stable run?

mike_r: yes — compared to baseline run 1797000000: H100 4096 b4 paged was ~6.0ms previously. So roughly 2x slowdown in this job.

devon_t: guess: our kernel-selection policy bumped paged for long seqs, but paged variant here ends up causing many small memcopies (prefetch thrash). Could also be different GRIDDIM/kblock for H100 warps.

sara: link to flame graph / trace? :link:

infra-bot: Trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood/s/1798129999/trace (nvvp + Nsight timelines)

ops-bot: CI perf job 1798129999 finished — artifacts at s3://rwd-infer-perf/1798129999/ (logs, traces, kernels)

jin: quick mitigation ideas:
- prefer flashv2 for H100 up to seq 6k (avoid paged fallthrough)
- increase KV prefetch buffer so fewer memcopies (reduce spill frequency)
- cap batch growth when seq > 2k to avoid multi-batch spill interaction

mike_r: tried a local policy tweak: prefer flashv2 for seq <= 6k on H100. Result: 4096 b4 from 12.4 -> 6.5ms (still ~10% above baseline). PR: https://git.redwood/r/attn-kern/132 (quick experiment)

devon_t: that's encouraging. Next: profile L2 cache / TLB / l2 miss counters and check kernel launch concurrency. I'll spin up targeted runs on h100-12 (p0 vs p1 power modes) to rule out power governor effects.

sara: also add vRAM allocator stats and per-request KV residency metric to the trace so we can see how long items are staying on GPU.

mike_r: will push updated benchmark with allocator counters and rerun tomorrow. tagging @jin for rollout decision once we have the full comparisons.

jin: thanks — if the flash-prefer policy holds across the power-mode sweep and A100/L40S are unaffected, suggest we ship a temporary kernel-policy override and follow with kernel-level micro-optimizations for paged memcopy pattern.

sara: noted. I'll file a perf ticket and attach these artifacts. :memo:

mike_r: filed PERF-987: "H100 seq>=4k KV-spill kernel regression — investigate paged memcpy thrash". Will update with next run IDs.

devon_t: assigning myself and mike_r for now. Will loop in runtime-schedulers if we need scheduler-side pacing.

mike_r: thanks — running the follow-up now, will post results here.
